assumption: This is a cost-threshold assessment. No SBSP result is expressed as a deployment-year forecast.
limitation: Official UK benchmarks may contain source publication years or commissioning references, but they are not used as SBSP scenarios.

assumption: All model financial inputs and outputs are 2024 real GBP. DCF values are discounted to the start of construction (t=0), and LCOE ends at the grid connection point.
limitation: External benchmarks with other price bases are labelled rather than silently harmonised.

assumption: Five stage efficiencies are explicit inputs; their product is the computed end-to-end efficiency. Stage powers are calculated backwards from fixed grid-delivered AC power.
limitation: Beam geometry, power-density limits, land, weather and detailed electrical design remain outside the simplified chain.

assumption: System specific mass is kg per kW delivered AC at the grid boundary, so orbital mass equals delivered kW times specific mass and is never divided by efficiency again.
limitation: The report's architecture-specific-power values can include manufacturer claims and remain architecture-specific; the model default is exploratory.

assumption: Programme contingency is applied once to pre-contingency initial CAPEX.
limitation: It is excluded from fixed O&M and replacement bases and does not replace a quantified risk register.

assumption: Space and ground replacement rates use separate eligible cost bases; space replacement includes proportional hardware, launch, transfer and assembly.
limitation: Annual-equivalent rates simplify discrete failures, spares, campaign scheduling and learning.

assumption: Renewable system-adjusted benchmarks use BEIS enhanced LCOE ranges from 2020 because the latest DESNZ 2025 LCOE report says wider system costs require full system modelling.
limitation: Values are in 2018 real GBP and should be treated as indicative ranges.

assumption: Nuclear is represented only by a public contract-price marker because recent DESNZ reports do not publish an updated generic nuclear LCOE.
limitation: Not directly comparable with 2024 real generation LCOE.

assumption: A threshold is necessary only within this model, its accounting boundary and the stated parameter ranges; it is not a universal engineering requirement.
limitation: Alternative architectures, coupled parameter changes or omitted system value can move the threshold.

assumption: Published SBSP cost estimates are used as context and consistency checks, not as validation or direct substitutes for this model's inputs.
limitation: Architectures, orbit destinations, price years, financing and cost boundaries differ materially across studies.

assumption: The real project discount rate is used in an explicit discounted-cash-flow LCOE; a CRF result is retained only as a secondary reconciliation metric.
limitation: It is not an observed SBSP WACC; taxes, inflation and financing tranches are not modelled.

assumption: The model ends at the grid connection point and uses a delivered capacity-factor proxy that combines availability, outages and operating constraints.
limitation: Downstream transmission reinforcement, balancing, storage, reliability services, curtailment and monetised system value are excluded.

assumption: The default four-year construction profile has equal annual shares at t=0 through t=3; commissioning is at t=4 and first operating-year energy is valued at t=5.
limitation: A project-specific engineering and procurement schedule could materially change financing effects.

assumption: Launch to the LEO staging boundary and incremental transfer to the architecture-dependent HEO operational orbit are separate. Per-kg and per-flight launch modes are mutually exclusive.
limitation: Neither the launch input nor a small transfer proxy is a commercial quotation for delivery to final orbit.

assumption: Efficiency, delivered-power-specific mass, hardware cost, launch cadence, replacement logistics and financing risk are not necessarily independent.
limitation: One-way and equal-fraction results are conditional mathematical comparisons, not probabilities or roadmaps.
